title: mypy: name rebinding in check_registry; migrate's git-vouch API unchecked
description:
mypy (no project config; --python-version 3.10, as mypy no longer accepts 3.9) is clean on git-vouch-attest and reports 20 errors in git-vouch and 5 in git-vouch-migrate. No runtime type confusion found, but two categories have a maintainability cost:

1. [assignment]/[misc] in git-vouch check_registry (1341-~2120, one ~800-line function with ~20 closures): names are rebound to different types in the same scope. others: list[Person] at 1546, list[str] at 1632, str at 2018; key: PersonKey at 1596, Optional[PersonKey] at 1686; gone: dict at 2084, set at 2085; e: exception binding (except ... as e, 1704/1709) reused as an Endorsement loop variable at 1984 and 2050. In the core trust-check function, a reader (or a later edit) can easily take one binding for another. Fix: distinct names (others_people / other_handles / claimants_text, dict ends vs set gone_tiers, err for exceptions).

2. [name-defined] git-vouch-migrate:103, 574, 864: annotations vouch.CheckResult / vouch.PersonKey / vouch.Person refer to a module loaded at runtime by _load_vouch (SourceFileLoader). The loader is runtime-sound (bytecode suppressed, nothing needs sys.modules), but vouch is ModuleType, so every vouch.* use in migrate is Any to a type checker: a rename or signature change in git-vouch breaks migrate only at runtime. Fix: accept it and say so in a ponytail: comment at _load_vouch, or add a typing.TYPE_CHECKING stub import so mypy resolves the names.
